name: Octans
introduction: is the Octant, a navigational instrument, introduced by Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille in the 1750s. It contains the south celestial pole, the point around which the southern sky turns.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Unlike the north, the south celestial pole has no bright pole star. Its closest naked-eye star, Sigma Octantis, is faint, about fifth magnitude, and difficult to see from anywhere with light pollution.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Nu Octantis](hip:107089) is an orange giant 63 light-years away and the brightest star. [Beta Octantis](hip:112405) and [Delta Octantis](hip:70638) complete the figure.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: Southern star-trail photographs circle a point in Octans. Earth’s slow wobble will carry the south celestial pole away from Octans over thousands of years, toward the bright stars of Carina and Vela, which will one day give the south a brilliant pole star.
